title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for Irrigation servicing
audience: Irrigation servicing operators, solo or with a team, who want repeat seasonal checks and referrals from clients they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask at the moment the client is most satisfied
instruction.body: Ask after the client confirms the system runs as expected, usually at the report sign-off or when the invoice is paid. Ask in one sentence, name the next step you would like, such as a review or the name of a neighbour with a system, and make it easy to say no. Record what you asked and what the client said. Timing matters: in one Baylor Keller Center experiment, a late reminder brought in more reviews than an immediate one (Baylor Keller Center, 1 June 2024). Google provides review links and QR codes for this purpose (Google Business Profile Help). Do not write reviews for clients or invent them. Filtering out unhappy clients is called review gating, which Podium, a vendor, says Google treats as a violation (Podium, 2 May 2022; not checked against Google's policy). Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer the next service before the client leaves
instruction.body: At the end of each visit, propose the next step with a date: a pre-season check before the growing season, a controller reschedule when the seasons change, or a second check after a repair. Clean Group's strata guide lists checking irrigation as a growing-season task, and says most strata properties need fortnightly maintenance from September to April (Clean Group, 9 March 2026). Put the scope, interval and price in writing, and confirm before the schedule changes. Check the electronic message rules before sending a written offer by email or text. ACMA says inferred consent is narrow and does not cover a message sent just after a purchase (ACMA, read 4 November 2026).

instruction.heading: Check in at the interval that suits the service
instruction.body: Schedule the check-in after the watering season has changed or after a repair, so the client can see whether the schedule still holds. The check asks whether the zones run on schedule, whether anything has changed and whether other work is needed. Keep it short and close the loop with a reply. A message that promotes a service can be commercial even when it is framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 9 November 2023, on ACMA enforcement). Check each message before sending.

instruction.heading: Re-contact previous clients before their busy periods
instruction.body: Plan a short message before the growing season starts in September, and before any change to the watering window that applies to the client's address. Offer only dates you can deliver, on written terms, with a clear way to opt out. Do not contact anyone who has asked not to hear from you. ACMA's guidance says an unsubscribe must be honoured within five working days, so record each opt-out as soon as you receive it and stop sending to that client (ACMA). At the end of the season, review the response and note which timing worked.

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide what you will offer, such as a credit on the next visit, and write down the condition for payment, normally that the referred person has completed a paid job. Give the referrer a copy, keep a record of each referral and whether the reward was paid, and never promise a reward you cannot deliver. Stating the reward in the invitation increased referrals across seven studies (Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research, 2023), so state it. Get the referred person's consent before any referral message is sent, because a referrer's word alone may not be enough (Clayton Utz, 11 May 2017; older source). The tax and contract effect of any reward is not confirmed here, so check it with an adviser before you start.

procedure: After each visit is signed off, make one review or referral request and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the next-service offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and confirm it with the client.
Schedule the check-in for the interval that suits the service, and send it using the electronic message rules.
Plan a re-contact message for each busy period in the calendar, and exclude anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward terms and the payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books, confirm the referred job is paid before applying the reward, and record the outcome.
Review at the end of each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: An irrigation client with a multi-zone system is happy with a seasonal check and says she will recommend the technician to her neighbour, who has a larger system with a reported fault.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the technician do before the neighbour books, and what should the technician avoid?
workedExamples.reasoning: The technician writes the reward terms and the payment condition before any referral: a credit on the next visit, applied once the neighbour completes a paid visit. The client passes on the neighbour's details, and the technician contacts the neighbour only if the neighbour agrees. The technician does not promise a reward that is not written down. The neighbour's reported fault is quoted separately, after the technician confirms that the repair is within scope and that the registration that applies in that state covers it. The technician does not accept plumbing work that the registration does not cover.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the result.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask after sign-off or payment, when the client has confirmed the result is right.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral reward that was never written down, so the terms are disputed later.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral is made, and give the referrer a copy.

commonErrors.error: Publishing a client's name, photo or review without their consent for that use.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each thing you plan to publish, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you, or using a re-contact message to pressure them.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list, honour it at once, and keep re-contact messages factual and optional.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. Do not write reviews on a client's behalf or invent them. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, client details are personal information. Coverage for a small business is not confirmed in this lesson, so check the OAIC's small business guidance.

Review platforms and referral programmes can have their own rules on incentives. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on the review's content. Check each platform's rules before offering any reward.

Check-in and re-contact messages sent by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when it is framed as a service reminder. Check each message before sending. The Act text was not read for this lesson.

A referral does not extend the licence, registration or insurance of the business that accepts the work. In Victoria, non-agricultural irrigation is a registered plumbing class. NSW irrigation licensing is not confirmed. Accept only the work your registration and insurance cover, in the state where it is done. This lesson does not grant any licence.
Backflow testing is not covered by any source found, and it is not offered in this lesson.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the result, and make it easy to say no.
Offer the next service in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral rewards and their payment conditions in writing before anyone refers.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask an irrigation client for a review or referral?
options: Before the job starts, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the result is right
Only when the client has sent you a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to publish a review with their name and a photo of the finished work. What do you need?
options: Their consent for the name and photo you plan to publish
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own judgement that the photo looks professional

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward for an irrigation client look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Decided and written in advance, with the condition for payment stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the lesson say to propose the next step for the client?
options: At the end of each job, with a date

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on review content.

Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: a late reminder brought more reviews than an immediate one.
Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; the Google position it describes was not checked against Google's own policy.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer reward in the invitation increased referrals. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a service reminder that promotes anything can be commercial.
ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 4 November 2026. Supports: unsubscribe honoured within five working days; inferred consent is narrow.

Clean Group, strata gardening guide, https://www.clean-group.com.au/?p=195299, updated 9 March 2026. Vendor source. Supports: checking irrigation as a growing-season task; fortnightly maintenance September to April.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam (ACMA)
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages need the recipient's consent; messages must identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message needs a free unsubscribe option honoured within five working days. Publisher: ACMA.
